JUDGMENT
The Director of Enforcement Directorate, represented by its Assistant Director, Government of
India, Ministry of Finance, Dept. of Revenue, Shanthinagar, K.H.Road, Bangalore has presented this
complaint u/s.200 Cr.P.C. r/w Sec.45, 3, 4 and 8(5) of PMLA Act, 2002 against one company and
Spl.C.C.316/2016 eight accused persons.
2. It is stated that Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 has been enacted by the Parliament to
prevent Money Laundering and to provide for confiscation of proceeds of the crime property.
3. It is contended that based upon the complaint dtd.3.5.2013, filed by one Sri.Vittesh Kumar, Chief
Regional Manager, United Bank of India, Bangalore registered office, Bangalore, before CBI, EOW,
Chennai and based upon the said complaint, CBI had registered FIR in RC.3/E/2013- CBI/EOW/
Chennai, on 4.5.2013 for the offences punishable u/s.120B r/w Sec.420, 467 & 471 of IPC and
Sec.13(2) r/w Sec.13(1)(d) of Prevention of Spl.C.C.316/2016 Corruption Act against the accused
persons, contending that during 2009, term loan of Rs.16 crores was sanctioned in favour of accused
No.1 company for the purpose of importing software from M/s.Logass Infosolutions, Dubai and
from M/s.Valuemart Info Technologies Ltd., Bangalore. Accused No.3 Sri.K.Sathyanarayana had
offered collateral security of his land measuring 1 acres 30 guntas situated at Sadarmangala village,
Bengaluru for the security of the said loan. But the investigation conducted by the CBI revealed that,
after borrowing the said loan and disbursement of the loan, same was transferred to the accounts of
Dubai based company and subsequently, it was diverted from Dubai to the accounts of other
companies floated by accused No.2, being the Spl.C.C.316/2016 managing director of accused No.1
company. It is stated that, purpose for which loan of Rs.16 crores was obtained, has not been
achieved and on the other hand, it has been misutilised for their own purposes by diverting the
funds from M/s. Logass Infosolutions accounts to that of Mohan Raju and others and thereby
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

diverted the funds and misutilised for other purposes. The details of various transfers have also been
incorporated in the complaint.
4. It is stated that, the CBI has submitted the charge sheet for the above said offences against the
accused, after having come to the conclusion that, loan of Rs.16 crores has been diverted for some
other purpose and thereby cheated the United Bank of India. After receipt of the final report
Spl.C.C.316/2016 from the CBI, Enforcement Directorate has registered ECIR in BG2009/2014
dtd.14.3.2014 and initiated investigation under PMLA. During the course of investigation, several
documents and depositions were obtained by the investigation officer.
5. It is contended that, during the course of investigation, I.O., has recorded the statement of
Accused No.2 Sri.G.Dhananjaya Reddy on 21.7.2014 as per Sec.50(2)&(3) of PMLA. In his
statement, he stated that, he being the managing director of accused No.1 company and also director
of AGS Infotech Ltd, M/s. GDR Media Limited and M/s. Bluestream Infotech Limited, had taken
loan of Rs.16 crores from United Bank of India and remitted total amount of Rs.16,91,75,115/- to the
account of Spl.C.C.316/2016 M/s. Logass Infosolutions, Dubai for the purpose of importing
software, during the period September - October 2009. He also stated that, out of the said amount,
M/s.Logass Infosolutions, had sent back Rs.12,62,92,000/- to the account of M/s. AGS Infotech
Ltd, another amount of Rs.3,46,48,000/- to the account of M/s.GDR Media Ltd., as he is the
director of both the companies. He stated that, the softwares were downloaded as different modules
and from GDR Media Ltd. They have downloaded two modules. He further stated that, out of the
said amount so received, from the account of GDR Media limited, the following disbursement were
made.

6. He further stated that, at present he does not own any immovable property in his name and also
in the name of his family members. Office premises of accused No.1 company was functioning in a
rented premises at 29/1, Beretina Agrahara, Spl.C.C.316/2016 Electronic City, Bangalore and since
he was not able to pay the rents, as per request of the owner, he vacated the premises in the Month
of January 2014.
7. It is further contended that on 18.3.2015, again Sri.G.Dhananjaya Reddy has given statement
stating that he was arrested by the CBI on 7.8.2014 and kept in jail custody till 3.3.2015 and now he
is on bail. He also revealed that, charge sheet have also been filed against him by the CBI, in the case
of M/s. AGS Infotech Ltd and in the case of M/s. Ignix Technologies Solutions Pvt.Ltd. On enquiry
he stated that, he wanted to purchase a controlling stake in M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt.
Ltd., a company of Sri.Sunjay Aryan. Some payments were made to him, but balance payments were
not Spl.C.C.316/2016 made. However, he had purchased the property in the name of M/s.Libra
Interactive Learning Pvt.Ltd., for a sum of Rs.95 Lakhs. Rs.75 Lakhs was paid in cash and he has
made remaining payments through cheque. But he could not make full payments and as such
original property documents is not handed over by the broker Sri.Shivram.

8. Accused No.3 Sri Sathyanarayana Kanumilli was summoned and examined on 11.7.2014 as per
Sec.50 of PMLA and in his statement he has disclosed about receipt of Rs.2.50 crores through
Mohan Raj of M/s. Biocity Technologies. Further statement of Accused No.4 Smt.G.Nirmala also
been recorded as per Sec.50 of PMLA. The statements of other accused persons have also been
recorded.
Spl.C.C.316/2016
9. It is stated that, as per the materials collected and informations disclosed by the accused No.2, out
of the diverted fund, property measuring 1 acre 16 guntas in Sy.No.372/2 situated at Attibele village
was purchased by accused No.2, in the name of M/s.Libra Interactive Learning Pvt.Ltd., for a sum of
Rs.95 Lakhs and it becomes proceeds of crime.
10. It is further stated that, after collecting all the materials, steps were taken to pass provisional
attachment order to attach the property measuring 1 acre 16 guntas as per Sec.5(1) of PMLA and
taken possession of the said property. The said order was placed before the Adjudicating Authority,
New Delhi for passing confirmation of attachment order as per Sec.8(3) of the Act. Accordingly,
Adjudicating Spl.C.C.316/2016 Authority by the order dtd.24.6.2015 has confirmed the provisional
attachment order.
11. It is further contended that all the accused persons have played a role with regard to acquiring
these proceeds of crime, by directly or indirectly in assisting accused No.2 and thereby each one
having conspiracy to acquire the proceeds of crime. All the members of the Conspiracy Team are
liable to be prosecuted as per Sec.3 & 4 of the Act. Investigation is still going on. Accordingly, filed
this complaint with a prayer to take cognizance of the complaint and to register a case against the
accused persons and to convict them in accordance with Sec.4 of the Act and to confiscate the
property.
12.After receipt of the charge sheet, my learned predecessor in office has taken cognizance
Spl.C.C.316/2016 of the offences and ordered to issue summons to
13. In response to the summons issued, accused No.1 to 9 appeared along with their advocates and
they were released on bail. Subsequently, accused No.8 was reported to be dead and hence the case
against him was closed as abated. Accused No.6 & 7 were discharged vide order dtd.18.1.2024. The
case against accused No.9 has been quashed as per orders passed in Crl.Petition No.12503/2022
dated 20.9.2023 by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka as such his name has been deleted vide order
dtd.6.1.2024.
14. Copies of complaint and other documents have been served to the accused. Charge for the
offence within the meaning of Sec.3 and punishable Spl.C.C.316/2016 u/s.4 of PMLA was framed
and readover to all the accused. They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
15. In order to prove the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution has examined the complainant
as PW1 and 6 additional witnesses as Pws.2 to 7 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.38.
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

16. Thereafter, statements as contemplated under Section 313 Cr.P.C. have been recorded by putting
the incriminating evidence available against each of the accused No.1 to 5 who are facing the trial.
They have given answers and that have been typed in the respective columns.
17. Accused have chosen to adduce oral evidence and examined one witness Sri.Shivram as
Spl.C.C.316/2016 DW1, but no documents are marked.
18. Heard the arguments of learned Special Public Prosecutor Sri. I.S.Pramod Chandra and learned
Senior counsel Sri.K.S.Javali and Sri.Shivaji H Mane for accused no.1 to 5.
19. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the complainant proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the property
measuring 1 acre 15 guntas in Sy.No.372/2 situated at Attibele village was acquired
by accused No.2 to 5, representing accused No.1 company, on behalf of M/s.Libra
Interactive Learning Pvt.Ltd., represented by one Sri.Sunjay Aryan out of proceeds of
loan amount of Rs.16 crores borrowed on behalf of accused No.1 company, claiming it
as untainted property and thereby Spl.C.C.316/2016 committed the offence of money
laundering within the meaning of Sec.3 and punishable u/s.4 of PML Act?
2. What order?
20. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : 'As per final order' for the following:
REASONS
21. POINT NO.1: The learned Special Public Prosecutor Sri.I.S.Pramod Chandra by taking through
the evidence of PW1, 6 & DW1 along with relevant documents, has submitted that, admittedly as per
the judgment passed in Spl.CC.No.313/2014 and the copy of the same is made available,
Spl.C.C.316/2016 accused no.2 to 5 representing accused No.1 company have committed a crime by
diverting the loan amount of Rs.16 crores which was borrowed from United Bank of India in the
year 2009, for the purpose of importing software from the Dubai based company, same is a
predicate offence as per schedule of PMLA and the same is sufficient to come to a conclusion that
there is a crime committed by them. He has admitted that accused No.6 to 9 have been discharged
on account of the fact that the charges against them are not proved in Spl.CC.No.313/2014.
22. It is further argued that, the property in question which has been acquired out of proceeds of
crime in the name of PW6 Sunjay Aryan, who was the Managing Director of M/s.Libra Interactive
Spl.C.C.316/2016 Learning Pvt.Ltd., on 21.6.2010, for a sum of Rs.95 Lakhs. The evidence of PW6
and DW1 plays a vital role with regard to acquiring this property out of proceeds of crime, by
claiming that money as untainted property. There was no reason for PW6 to come and give a false
evidence stating that accused No.2 Sri.Dhananjayareddy has invested all the money for purchasing
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

this property in the name of his company. If he had purchased the property from out of his own
money, he could have very well claimed that property as his own property and made the
complainant not to file this complaint. He has categorically deposed as to how and in what manner
accused No.2 has misused him and made him to establish his own company, that too, in his own
complex and accused No.2 himself used to Spl.C.C.316/2016 manage the whole affairs including
banking transactions, through his auditor and clerk and also with regard to investing of Rs.95 lakhs
for acquiring this property out of proceeds of crime. He has categorically deposed that, he is only a
name sake purchaser but, he did not exercise any right over that property, at any point of time and
also he did not receive the original sale deed and he has given statement before the ED., stating that,
he is not the owner of that property. Nothing important has been elicited in his cross examination,
to discord his oral testimony. On the other hand, the suggestions made in his cross-examination and
the manner in which accused No.2 has examined DW1 who is actually complainant witness, clearly
shows that, there was an involvement of accused No.2, while Spl.C.C.316/2016 purchasing this
property out of the proceeds of crime. The evidence of DW1 is contrary to the recitals in the sale
deed ie., Ex.P18(a). If his evidence is carefully perused, it clearly indicates that he was in touch with
accused No.2 and he has given this false evidence at the instance of accused No.2. No suggestion has
been made in the cross examination of PW6 to the effect that, cash amount of Rs.75 lakhs has not
been paid by PW6. So all these circumstances clearly establish that, accused No.2 by creating his
own circumstances, by using his intelligent mind, had invested the proceeds of loan amount and
made PW6 to establish the company and then to purchase this property in his name. Therefore it
becomes proceeds of crime and hence accused No.2 to 5 are Spl.C.C.316/2016 liable to be punished
under PMLA.
23. On the other hand, learned Sr. Counsel Sri.K.S.Javali and Sri.Shivaji H Mane have argued that,
absolutely there is no materials collected by the complainant and placed before this court to hold
that, the property in question was purchased out of the alleged proceeds of loan amount. It is argued
that, this court has already observed during the course proceedings that, it is the duty of the
complainant to establish that this property was acquired out of that loan amount, which is called as
proceeds of crime by claiming that it is untainted property. Admittedly, there is no direct evidence to
show the involvement of either accused no.2 or accused No.3 to 5. Nothing has been placed to show
that, accused no.2 or 3 to 5 were present in Spl.C.C.316/2016 any manner, with regard to acquiring
of this property either during the course of sale talks or at the time of registration of the document.
Complainant has failed to collect bank accounts and other related documents, either from accused
no.1 company or from M/s.Libra Interactive Learning Pvt.Ltd., M/s. GDR Media Ltd and AGS
company, to show that funds were diverted from the accounts of accused No.1 company to the
account of M/s.Libra Interactive Learning Pvt.Ltd. In a case of this nature, complainant cannot
expect that, court of law should draw inference and it should decide the alleged criminal liability on
assumptions and presumptions. Even the statements u/s.50(2) & (3) of PMLA are recorded without
placing any proof, and hence those statements cannot be used as the Spl.C.C.316/2016 evidence to
prove the alleged guilt of the accused.
24. It is further argued that, inference can be drawn by court of law, only if initial burden is
discharged by the prosecution, with regard to investment of money made on behalf of accused No.1
or individually from the account of accused No.2 to 5 to the accounts of M/s.Libra Interactive
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

Learning Pvt.Ltd., for the purpose of acquiring this property, claiming that it is untainted property.
But here in this case, as per the evidence of PW1, 2 & 6, absolutely nothing has been placed to prove
the initial burden. Therefore, there is no obligation on the part of accused No.2 to 5, to give any
explanation. However, they have examined DW1, who is actually witness of the complainant, just to
show that, accused No.2 to 5 have not at all Spl.C.C.316/2016 involved in the alleged sale
transaction. Therefore, viewed from any angle, when there is no iota of materials collected by the
investigating agency to prove the initial burden, it is wrong on the part of the complainant to argue
that, accused No.2 to 5 have acquired this property out of alleged proceeds of loan amount.
25. The learned Senior counsel Sri.K.S.Javali for the accused has also cited the following decisions. I
have carefully perused the said judgments.
1. 2022 SCC Online SC 929 - Vijay Madanlal Choudhary & ors. Vs. Union of India and Ors.
2. (2018) 11 scc 1 - Nikesh Tarachand Shah Vs.Union of India and another.
3. Crl.Revision No.2536/2022 - Hari Shankar Gurjar and anr Vs.Directrate of Enforcement by High
Court of Madhya Pradesh Spl.C.C.316/2016
4. 2018 SCC Online Del.11078 - Himachal EMTA Power Ltd Vs. Union of India and others.
5. Crl.Petition No.10026/2023 - Mr. Dennis Sagaya Jude Vs. The Directorate of Enforcement and
another.
6. (2007) 4 SCC 70 - SMS Pharmaceuticals Ltd. Vs. Neeta Bhalla and another.
7. (2022) 15 SCC 430 - Ravindranatha Bajpe Vs. Mangalore Special Economic Zone Ltd & ors.
8. Crl.OP No.26898/2017 - R.Chandrasekaran Vs. ED passed by High Court of Judicature, Madras.
Dtd.20.1.2022
9. (1975) 4 SCC 664- Ashok Dulichand Vs. Mdahavlal Dube and anr.
10. (2000) 9 SCC 241 - State of Rajasthan & Ors.Vs. Khemraj & Ors.
11. (2007) 5 SCC 730 - J.Yoshoda Vs. K.Shobha Rani.
12. (2010) 4 SCC 491 - LIC of India & Anr. Vs. Rampal Singh Bisen.
13. (2010) 9 SCC 712 - M.Chandra Vs. Spl.C.C.316/2016 M.Thangamuthu & another.
14. (2011)4 SCC 240 : AIR 2011 SCC 1492 - H.Siddiqui Vs. A. Ramalingam.
15. (2016) 16 SCC 483 - Rakesh Mohindra Vs. Anita Beri and another.

16. 2012 SCC Online Kar.7228 - Vasanth Madhava Vs. E.Sheshadri.
17. (2023) 15 SCC 91 - Pavana Dibbur Vs. Directorate of Enforcement
18. (2004) 11 SCC 576 - AS.Krishna & others Vs. State of Kerala.
19. 1993 Supp (2) SCC 497 - Joti Parshad Vs. State of Haryana.
20. (2021) 6 SCC 707 - Opto Circuits India Ltd. Vs. Axis Bank and others
21. (2023) 4 SCC 357 - Rana Ayyub Vs. Directorate of Enforcement.
22. WP.No.32956/2024 - Dr.Natesh DB Vs. Directorate of Enforcement.
26. In the light of the said arguments and the Spl.C.C.316/2016 materials placed by the prosecution
and the accused persons, let me examine the facts and the evidence.
27. This court is required to discuss as to whether the property in question bearing Sy.No.373/2
measuring 1 acre 15 guntas, situated at Attibele Village was purchased for valuable consideration of
Rs.95 lakhs through a registered sale deed dtd.21.6.2010 in the name of M/s.Libra Interactive
Learning Pvt.Ltd., represented by its Managing Director Sri.Sunjay Aryan, who has been examined
as PW6, out of the proceeds of the loan, borrowed in the name of accused No.1 company from
United Bank of India, in the year 2009 by laundering the amount through different companies.
Spl.C.C.316/2016
28. Sec. 3 of the Act deals with money laundering which says as under:
Whosoever directly or indirectly attempts to indulge or knowingly assists or
knowingly is a party or is actually involved in any process or activity connected with
the 1[proceeds of crime including its concealment, possession, acquisition or use and
projecting or claiming] it as untainted property shall be guilty of offence of
money-laundering.
2[Explanation.--For the removal of doubts, it is hereby clarified that,--
(i) a person shall be guilty of offence of money-laundering if such person is found to
have directly or indirectly attempted to indulge or knowingly assisted or knowingly is
a party or is actually involved in one or more of the following processes or activities
connected with proceeds of crime, namely:--
(a) concealment; or
(b) possession; or Spl.C.C.316/2016
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

(c) acquisition; or
(d) use; or
(e) projecting as untainted property; or
(f) claiming as untainted property, in any manner whatsoever;
(ii) the process or activity connected with proceeds of crime is a continuing activity
and continues till such time a person is directly or indirectly enjoying the proceeds of
crime by its concealment or possession or acquisition or use or projecting it as
untainted property or claiming it as untainted property in any manner whatsoever.]
As per the judgment in Vijay Madanlal Choudary and all other decisions cited, there
must be a crime which is a scheduled offence and out of that crime, money should be
generated and laundered for the purpose of acquiring the property, having possession
etc. As per my observations during the course of proceedings on 22.8.2024 which
reads as under:
Spl.C.C.316/2016 It is to be noted that, in the last occasion this court has indicated
that the complainant / E.D. to ascertain as to who are the witnesses who are relevant
to decide the issue involved, are to be examined. But today the E.D. has not appeared
and submitted any applications in that regard. It is be noted that, in this case only
one property is involved and according to the complainant it was acquired out of
proceeds of crime.
Since predicate offence is proved and there is a judgment in that regard, production
of the certified copy of that judgment would serve a purpose to show that there was a
crime and that has been proved.
Now the question before this court is whether A.2 to 5 are in any related to M/S Libra
Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., represented by Sri.Sunjay Aryan, in whose
Spl.C.C.316/2016 name the property was purchased, and the proceeds of loan
amount which was diverted, in any way was invested to purchase this property.
In the complaint, names of relevant witnesses have been not been cited. However,
subsequently memo has been filed by showing additional 8 witnesses and that was
allowed.
Out of the said 8 witnesses 4 witnesses have been examined.
In view of the above, in order to decide the issue involved in the case at the earliest
point of time, the Assistant Director of E.D., Bengaluru is directed to examine the
matter in the light of the said observation, within 5 days and to submit the memo as
to, to whom they wish to examine to prove the above said issue.
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

This observation has been made, having regarding to the facts and the crux
Spl.C.C.316/2016 involved and in order to dispose of the matter at the earliest and
not with any other intension.
It is to be noted that, the complainant is required to place primafacie materials to
show that, the funds acquired out of loan amount which was borrowed being
directors / Managing Director, money was laundered and invested on this property
and got registered in the name of M/s.Libra Interactive Learning Pvt.Ltd.,
represented by PW6.
29. In the complaint, the complainant has given some chart with regard to flow of money from the
account of GDR Media Ltd to the account of Sunjay Aryan and M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt.
Ltd., and other companies.
Spl.C.C.316/2016
30. Admittedly, this property was not purchased either in the name of A.1 company or in the name
of accused No.2 to 5. Now on account of the fact that accused No.6 to 9 have been acquitted in
Spl.CC.313/2014, they have been discharged. Therefore the charge framed in this case is required to
be modified and accordingly modified as under:
Whether the complainant / prosecution proves that the property in question was
representing accused No.1 company, out of proceeds of crime loan amount of Rs.16
crores, borrowed in the name of accused no.1 during the year 2009 from United Bank
of India by laundering the same through various accounts and in the name of M/s.
Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., represented by Sunjay Aryan being the
Spl.C.C.316/2016 managing director and it becomes the proceeds of crime within the
meaning of Sec.3 ?
31. To answer this charge, prosecution has examined PW1 who has conducted investigation. PW1
Sri.C.Vijay Kumaran, Retired Assistant Director, ED. His evidence would show that on the basis of
the charge sheet documents submitted by the CBI, relating to RC 03/E/2013 - CBI/ EOW/Chennai,
ECIR in BGZ009/2014 was registered and received the documents as per Ex.P1 to 9, 14 to 17 etc. He
has also recorded the statements of some of the accused persons and others as per Sec.50(2)& (3) of
PMLA.
32. It is to be noted that in the cross- examination, many suggestions were made with
Spl.C.C.316/2016 regard to the manner in which investigation was conducted. He has categorically
admitted that, he has not at all collected the documents with regard to GDR Media Ltd., AGS
Company, M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., and also not recorded the statements of
officials of United Bank of India. He also admitted that, he has not conducted investigation with
regard to FEMA violations. He stated that he cannot answer to a question that, if that amount was
not utilised for that purpose for which loan was taken, documents referred in Ex.P3 would not have
come.
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

33. It is to be noted that this court in Spl.CC 313/2014 has given answer to all the questions with
regard to FEMA, FERA and Sec.420 of IPC etc. The Judgment of that case is sufficient to come to a
Spl.C.C.316/2016 conclusion that, accused No.2 to 5 representing accused No.1 company have
committed fraud by not utilising the loan amount for the purpose for which it was sanctioned and
also by offering a property as security by accused No.3 Sathyanarayana, even though, it was not
available on that day, to offer it as a collateral security. So to the effect that they have committed a
crime of defrauding the bank and it is proved. But the fact remains in this case is, whether the
proceeds of that loan amount was utilised by accused No.2 to 5 for the purpose of acquiring that
property in the name of M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., represented by Sunjay Aryan who
has been examined as PW6. But if the entire materials placed by the complainant including the
statements Spl.C.C.316/2016 u/s.50(2)&(3) of PMLA are carefully perused, court is not in a position
to come to a conclusion that there are circumstances which shows that money had flown from the
account of either of A.1 company or from the account of A2 to 5 or from the account of GDR Media
Ltd and AGS company. Interestingly, complainant has not taken pains to ascertain the true facts and
to make GDR Media Ltd., AGS company and M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., as accused
persons in the case. If the evidence of PW1 is carefully perused, it clearly indicates that, only on the
basis of the charge sheet submitted in the predicate office case and by utilising the provisions under
PMLA and without understanding as to the proceedures regarding conducting investigation to
ascertain the Spl.C.C.316/2016 true facts, he had submitted an application for passing provisional
attachment order as per Sec.5 of the Act through PW2 and thereafter, got it confirmed through
adjudicating authority u/s.8 and then filed the complaint. It is to be noted that, in a criminal trail,
there is no scope for drawing assumptions and presumptions. Charge must be proved by the
prosecution in accordance with law. Sec.24 of PMLA comes in to picture only, if initial burden is
discharged. There is no concept of conclusive proof and unrebutable presumption and only if some
material is collected and placed before the court to show flowing of money as alleged in the
complaint and purchasing of the property, out of the money which was stated to have been
laundered and it is out of proceeds of crime, then Spl.C.C.316/2016 only, accused are responsible to
give rebutable evidence to show that it was not purchased out of proceeds of crime.
34. In this regard the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paras 308 & 309 in
Vijaya Madanlal Choudhary case, becomes relevant which reads as under:
308. The fact that the proceeds of crime have been generated as a result of criminal
activity relating to a scheduled offence, which incidentally happens to e a non-
cognizable offence, would make not difference. The person is not prosecuted for the scheduled
offence by invoking provisions of the 2002 Act, but only when he hs derived or obtained property as
a result of criminal activity relating to or in relation to a scheduled offence and the indulges in
Spl.C.C.316/2016 process or activity connected with such proceeds of crime.
309. ..The offence under this Act in terms of Sec.3 is specific to involvement in any process or
activity connected with the proceeds of crime which is generated as a result of criminal activity
related to the schedule offence.
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

35. In order to prove that accused No.2 Sri.Dhananjayareddy has invested the alleged proceeds of
crime through his other accounts, to purchase the property under sale deed marked as ExP18(a),
complainant has examined the purchaser of that property who was representing M/s. Libra
Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., as PW6. Of course, he has deposed that when he had come to
Bangalore in search of job, he came in contact with accused Spl.C.C.316/2016 No.2 and he asked for
experience certificate in order to go to abroad, but accused No.2 prevailed over him to stay back and
allowed him to establish M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., in his own premises and
accordingly, he was running his business, but accused No.2 himself used to look after all the
accounts through his auditor. He also deposed that he has not invested any money to purchase this
property and he was not the person who was interested in purchasing this property and he did not
negotiate for purchasing this property. On the other hand, accused no.2 himself got purchased the
property, by investing his own money, but in the name of M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd.
The cross-examination conducted by learned counsel for the accused discloses that,
Spl.C.C.316/2016 this witness admitted that, M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., was his
private limited company, registered under Companies Act, 1956 and he had 90% share and his wife
had 10% share. He also admitted all the suggestions with regard to maintaining of books of
accounts, audit etc. Even though he stated that his signatures were taken on blank cheques by the
person from accused No.2, but, he has not produced any documents to substantiate the said
contention. No document was confronted to him by ED authority, while recording his statement as
per Ex.P25. Even PW1 has also not secured any documents pertaining to M/s. Libra Interactive
Learning Pvt. Ltd. He admitted that the property has been registered in his name and the amounts
were paid from out of his accounts. Even Spl.C.C.316/2016 though he stated that, cash amounts of
Rs.25 Lakhs each on 3 occasions were paid by accused No.2 himself, but there is no believable and
acceptable materials collected and produced in that regard.
36. It is to be noted that, this property was purchased on 21.6.2010 and ED has examined him in the
year 2015. During that 5 years period, he did not do anything either to issue notice to accused no.2
or to any body stating that, since he had purchased the property, he has to take recourse to get
transfer the property in his name or to the names of anybody or company. Since PW1 has not
collected any documents pertaining to M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., in order to show
that any amount was transferred from the accounts of accused No.1 or from the accounts of accused
no.2 Spl.C.C.316/2016 to 5, the assertion made by PW1 on the basis of predicate offence case result,
does not inspire the confidence of court of law. Because, when particular charge is levelled against
the accused persons, u/s.3 of PMLA, the first and foremost thing required to be established is, that
there was proceeds of crime and it was laundered through different modes and invested the same for
acquiring this property. Then it becomes the proceeds of crime and untainted property. But as
stated above and as rightly pointed by learned Senior counsel Sri.Kiran S. Javali, absolutely there is
no iota of materials collected and placed before this court either by PW1 or by PW2. If the evidence
of PW1 is carefully perused, it clearly shows that, his evidence is based upon assumptions and
presumptions which is not Spl.C.C.316/2016 permissible under criminal jurisprudence. What
prevented him to collect the relevant materials to show the flow of money from one account to
another account in order to show the important aspect of money laundering, has not been explained
at all. At the cost of repetition, it is to be noted that, just because this court has already convicted
accused No.1 to 5 in predicate offence case, on the ground that, they have cheated the bank by not
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

repaying the loan amount, there is no scope under PMLA or any other law for the time being in
force, to draw an inference to the effect that, the said loan amount was utilised for acquiring this
property by claiming it, as untainted property. Particularly, when this property has not been
purchased either in the name of accused No.1 Spl.C.C.316/2016 company or in the names of accused
No.2 to 5, and when accused No.1 to 5 are not claiming any sort of right relating to this property,
heavy burden is on the complainant to place legally acceptable materials in order to draw an
inference that accused No.1 to 5 have invested the money to purchase this property in the name of
M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., represented by PW6. The evidence of PW6, PW1 & 2
cannot be accepted as gospel truth to come to a conclusion that accused No.1 to 5 have played a role
while purchasing this property. Therefore, in the absence of any iota of materials, atleast to draw an
inference that accused No.2 had participated with regard to the transactions taken place while
purchasing this property, it is not at all possible for Spl.C.C.316/2016 this court of law to believe and
accept the arguments of learned SPP.
37. The prosecution also wants to rely upon some stray answers given by DW1 with regard to his
acquaintance with accused No.2. DW1 in fact, was cited as prosecution witness, but he was not
examined. However, in order to clarify certain things, accused have examined him. He is a retired
BEL Employee and he has deposed that he negotiated the sale transaction. His evidence would only
go to show that sale negotiation was made by him between Sunjay Aryan and the sellers. He has
given contrary evidence with regard to the payment of consideration amount. According to him,
cash amount of Rs.75 lakhs has not at all been paid to the seller. He admitted that only two cheques
for Spl.C.C.316/2016 Rs.5 Lakhs each were encashed and other two cheques have become
dishonoured. His evidence would show that he has retained the original sale deed with him on
account of the fact that remaining amount of Rs.85 Lakhs was not paid by Sunjay Aryan.
38. It is to be noted that the evidence of this witness, if carefully perused, coupled with Ex.P18(a), it
shows that no body can imagine that this type of transaction take place in this modern days. The sale
deed was executed on 21.6.2010, but he stated that even now Rs.85 Lakhs has not been paid.
Admittedly, sellers have not initiated any proceedings either to recover the alleged balance amount
of Rs.85 lakhs or to get cancel the registered sale deed on any ground. No fool would
Spl.C.C.316/2016 keep quite for all these years without taking any action, if so much of the amount
that too in the year 2010 has not been paid. Therefore the evidence of this witness does not inspire
the confidence of the court and it will not benefit the case of both the parties in any manner. The
only admission elicited is that, after PW6 was examined he met accused no.2, does not enure to the
benefit of prosecution to establish the contention that accused No.2 has involved in the sale
transaction and he had in fact, has paid consideration amount to purchase the property in the name
of PW6. As stated above, in a criminal charge, initial burden is always on the prosecution to place
believable and acceptable materials, then only, court can ask the accused to give explanation. Here
in this case, Spl.C.C.316/2016 accused are not at all claiming any sort of right over the property in
question. Moreover, when the complainant has not placed any materials to show that accused No.1
to 5 are related to this property and directly or indirectly they have played a role while purchasing
this property and when this very important aspect is not proved by the prosecution, the alleged
statements recorded u/s.50 of PMLA cannot be relied upon as a gospel truth, to come to a
conclusion that there was a money laundering taken place out of loan proceeds and it was used as
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

untainted property to purchase this property. As rightly pointed out by learned Sr.counsel
Sri.K.S.Javali, the complainant has failed to make GDR Media Ltd., AGS company and Libra
Interactive Learning Pvt. Ltd., companies as parties to the Spl.C.C.316/2016 proceedings.
Admittedly the books of accounts have not been recovered from the office of the said companies.
Therefore, from some bank statements to show that, some amounts were withdrawn from the
accounts of GDR Media, the court cannot come to a conclusion that the said amount was utilised for
purchasing this property.
39. It is to be noted that it is a mistry as to how and in what manner this property was purchased.
Complainant has failed to find out the link between the transactions and generation of funds to
acquire this property. What prevented the complainant to collect all these important materials to
show the chain of link with regard to the investment and the alleged proceeds of crime, has not been
explained at all. In a case of this nature, Spl.C.C.316/2016 particularly property is not standing in
the name of the accused persons and particularly when they are not claiming any sort of right over
the property, heavy burden cast upon the prosecution to establish the fact with regard to money
laundering. But prosecution for the reasons best known to it, simply relied upon the investigation
conducted by CBI with regard to bank loan transaction to make the court to believe it as a gospel
truth and to claim that there was a money laundering and out of that, this property was purchased.
This type of casual approach on the part of the prosecution cannot be appreciated by the court of
law. When the court is required to conduct criminal trial to punish any person under PMLA, strong
and admissible evidence was required to be collected and placed before the Spl.C.C.316/2016 court
for proper appreciation. But, for the reasons best known to PW1, he has failed to make sincere
efforts to ascertain the true facts and also to make all the companies as parties.
40. In view of the said factual situation, involved in this case, the decisions cited on behalf of the
accused need not be examined in detail. Because the very fact that money laundering is not proved,
hence question of proving the charge against accused No.1 to 5 does not arise at all. Prosecution has
miserably failed to place cogent, convincing and satisfactory evidence to prove the charges.
Therefore Sec.24 of PMLA does not operate and hence question of giving rebutal evidence by the
accused persons does not arise at all. Therefore, I am not inclined to accept the Spl.C.C.316/2016
arguments of learned SPP. Hence, I answer the above point in the negative.
41.POINT NO.2: The next point for consideration is, what is required to be done with regard to the
property involved. In this regard Sec.8(7) of PMLA, becomes relevant and it reads as under:
Where the trial under this Act cannot be conducted by reason of the death of the
accused or the accused being declared a proclaimed offender or for any other reason
or having commenced but could not be concluded, the Special Court shall, on an
application moved by the Director or a person claiming to be entitled to possession of
a property in respect of which an order has been passed under sub-section (3) of
section 8, pass appropriate orders regarding confiscation or release of the property,
as the case may be, involved in the offence of Spl.C.C.316/2016 money-laundering
after having regard to the material before it.]
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

42. As per the said provision this court is empowered to take a decision having regard to the
material available, for disposal of the property. The United Bank of India has filed an application
under the said provision with a request to release this property in their favour for the purpose of
adjusting the proceeds towards the loan amount, which was borrowed by A.1 company. But in view
of my above findings, since the complainant has failed to prove that the property has been acquired
as untainted property, out of the alleged proceeds of crime by laundering. Therefore, it is not
possible for the court to release the property infavour of the bank.
43. As discussed above the original sellers of Spl.C.C.316/2016 the property for all these 15 years,
have not made any attempt to claim their rights over the property on the ground that consideration
amount has not been paid. If really the consideration amount was not paid by PW6, the sellers
would not have kept quite for all these years without making any claim before any court of law,
either to recover the balance amount or to seek cancellation of the registered sale deed. The silence
on the part of the sellers that too for all these 15 years, and particularly when the people are finding
some cause of action to make a claim over any property, would show that they had sold the property
in favour of PW6 after having collected the consideration amount of Rs.95 Lakhs before and after
the execution of the registered sale deed.
Spl.C.C.316/2016 Therefore, they have lost their rights over the property.
44. Admittedly, A.1 to 5 are not making any claim over the property. So the only person who is
entitled to make a claim over the property is PW6 Sri.Sunjay Aryan. But for the reasons best known
to him, he also abandoned his claim by making a categorical statement before the ED authority and
also before this court on oath stating that, he has no manner of rights over that property since he has
not invested any money to purchase the property. It shows that under some misterious
circumstances, this property must have been purchased in the name of PW6 who was representing a
company, out of some ill-gotten money by somebody else, but having apprehension of criminal law
in motion, they Spl.C.C.316/2016 must have thought fit to give up their claim over the property.
Otherwise, either PW6 or any other person who stated to have invested the money to purchase this
property would have come forward to make a claim over the property. God only knows as to who
actually invested the money to purchase this property. Because the complainant has not made best
efforts to ascertain the chain of link with regard to flow of money to purchase the property.
However, the complainant has become successful to make either PW6 or some body who had
actually invested the money to understand the situation and to give up their claim in relation to the
property. This is very classic case where, no body is ready to make a claim over the property having
regard to seriousness of the PMLA.
Spl.C.C.316/2016
45. So under the said circumstances, since the only person in law is competent to make a claim over
the property ie., PW6 himself has given up his claim and made it very clear that he has not invested
any money to purchase the property, the law of escheat would come in to operation, in order to
confiscate the property infavour of Central Government, because, when no body is making a claim
over the property, ultimately the Government becomes the owner under the said Law of Escheat.
Directorate Of Enforcement vs Ms Nexxoft Infotel Ltd on 10 February, 2025

Atleast to this effect the complainant has succeeded and that is appreciable one.
46. The learned Senior Counsel Sri.K.S.Javali has argued that since M/s. Libra Interactive Learning
Private Limited has not been made as party, property cannot be confiscated because,
Spl.C.C.316/2016 money laundering is not proved. But, the said arguments on behalf of accused no.1
to 5 cannot be accepted, for the simple reason that they have no locus standi over the property. Just
because M/s. Libra Interactive Learning Private Limited, is not made as party, even though it is a
technical issue, but since the owner of the said company ie., PW6 himself came and given categorical
statement on oath, stating that he has no right over the property, that technicality does not come in
the way of this court to take a decision with regard to confiscation of the property, having regard to
Sec.8(7) of PMLA, 2002.
47. In view of my above discussion and having regard to the peculiar circumstances involved in the
case, and the scope of Sec.8(7) of PMLA, I am of the Spl.C.C.316/2016 clear opinion the principles of
Law of Escheat shall be invoked and ordered to confiscate the property in favour of Central
Government. It is made clear that it is for the Central Government to take a decision as to whether
the property should be auctioned in public auction or to retain it for any purpose and in case if it is
sold in public auction, the proceeds may be given to the United Bank of India, which is also a public
undertaking and dealing with public money, or not. With these observations, I proceed to pass the
following:
ORDER Acting U/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C., I hereby acquit the accused No.1 to 5 of the
offence within the meaning of Sec.3 and punishable u/s.4 of PML Act, 2002.
Spl.C.C.316/2016 The bail bonds of accused no.2 to 5 and that of their surety shall
stand cancelled.
The property measuring 1 acre 16 guntas in Sy.No.372/2 situated at Attibele village,
shall be confiscated to Central Government in terms of the observations made in para
47 of the judgment.
